remnawave_nginx.options_hint: How the real client IP is passed to Xray. The main port 443 serves both direct clients and CDN — the options below only define where nginx takes the IP from. The X-Forwarded-For header is always overwritten — clients cannot spoof it.
remnawave_nginx.xray_requirements: For Xray to accept the IP from the header: the inbound must have sockopt.trustedXForwardedFor = ["X-Forwarded-For"], listen on 127.0.0.1, and the Xray core must be recent (correct for gRPC since v26.6.22, older cores ignore the header). Otherwise stats keep showing 127.0.0.1 — see the page help for details.
remnawave_nginx.cdn_ranges_hint: The client-IP header is only accepted from these ranges. 0.0.0.0/0 = trust everyone: anyone can spoof their IP with a single header — use deliberately.
remnawave_nginx.pp_hint: A dedicated listen port with proxy_protocol — HAProxy only (clients and CDN keep using 443: nginx cannot mix PP and plain connections on one port). Empty IP = accept the PROXY header from anyone — then make sure to firewall the port.
remnawave_nginx.fallback_url: Where to send the rest of the traffic (fallback)
remnawave_nginx.fallback_url_hint: Anything that doesn't match the rules, plus Xray errors (502/503/504), is proxied here — from the outside the server looks like a regular site. Empty — nginx will return 404.
remnawave_nginx.acme_hint: ACME opens /.well-known/acme-challenge/ — Let's Encrypt uses it to verify domain ownership when issuing and renewing a certificate over HTTP. Not needed for wildcard certificates: those are verified via a DNS record. The redirect works only if port 80 is open in the firewall.
remnawave_nginx.options_rebuild_warning: Applying options rebuilds the config from the template (rules survive, manual edits do not)
remnawave_nginx.raw_config_warning: The {DOMAIN} placeholder (in double curly braces) is replaced with the node's domain during sync. Manual edits outside the LOCATIONS markers survive rule changes.

xray_test.reason_CORE_START_FAILED: Core failed to start — check the key parameters
xray_test.reason_PROXY_HANDSHAKE_FAILED: Traffic does not pass through the proxy
xray_test.reason_HTTP_TIMEOUT: Request through the proxy timed out

xray_test.fill_name_and_payload: Fill in the name and the content
xray_test.fill_name_and_sni: Fill in the name and the SNI list
xray_test.core_not_downloaded: Core not downloaded yet — it will be fetched on the first check
xray_test.full_mode_hint: Without it — only DNS resolution and a TCP connection, the core is not started
xray_test.tls_inspect_hint: Who issued the masking domain's certificate: an unexpected issuer hints at interception
xray_test.client_hwid_off: no HWID — some panels will not return keys
xray_test.pick_location: Pick at least one place to run from
xray_test.sync_host_hint: Needed when the key's transport Host equals the SNI — otherwise the server answers 404
xray_test.include_original_sni: Also test the config's own SNI
xray_test.include_original_sni_hint: The key is tested as-is first, then with each domain from the list. Without it there is nothing to compare against: if every domain fails, you cannot tell filtering from a dead server.
xray_test.hint_CERT_MISMATCH: The server certificate is issued for a different domain. For REALITY this means the server rejected the masking parameters — check the public key, short id and SNI.
xray_test.hint_CERT_UNTRUSTED: The server certificate fails verification: expired, self-signed or issued by an unknown authority.
xray_test.hint_CONN_REFUSED: The server refused the connection on this port — the port is closed, the service is down, or the address is wrong.
xray_test.hint_CONN_RESET: The server dropped the connection. Usually a reply to wrong credentials, or the link is being cut by the provider.
xray_test.hint_IO_TIMEOUT: The server did not answer in time. It may be overloaded, unreachable from this location, or blocked on the way.
xray_test.hint_DNS_FAIL: The server domain does not resolve — check the address in the key.
xray_test.hint_AUTH_FAILED: The server rejected the credentials — the UUID or password in the key does not match.
xray_test.hint_REALITY_REJECTED: The server rejected the REALITY handshake — the public key, short id or SNI do not match.
xray_test.hint_PROTOCOL_MISMATCH: A different protocol answers on this port than the key declares — check the port and connection type.
xray_test.hint_NO_ROUTE: There is no route to the server from this point — most likely a network-level block.
xray_test.hint_GRPC_UNAVAILABLE: The server does not accept the gRPC connection: check serviceName in the key and that this port really serves gRPC rather than plain TLS.
xray_test.hint_HANDSHAKE_STALLED: The server accepted the connection but never answered the handshake. For REALITY that is normal behaviour with wrong parameters: check the public key, short id and SNI. The other option is filtering on the way that throttles the connection.
xray_test.sni_own_hint: The key's own SNI — the one that came in the subscription or link. The other rows are substituted from your list and should be compared against this one.
xray_test.reason_EXIT_IP_UNKNOWN: Works, but the exit IP is unknown
xray_test.hint_SLOW_RTT: Traffic passes, but latency is over 1.5 s — such a key is uncomfortable to use. Usually distant geography, an overloaded server or a narrow link.
xray_test.hint_EXIT_IP_UNKNOWN: The connectivity check passed, but the service reporting the exit address did not answer. Servers that filter part of their outbound traffic behave like this: the key works, but not for every site.
xray_test.filter_blocked_hint: The server port answers but traffic does not pass — the typical picture of DPI filtering: the TCP handshake goes through and the connection itself is throttled. Explicit failures (closed port, wrong certificate, bad key) are not counted here.
xray_test.reason_DPI_BLOCK: Looks like filtering on the way
xray_test.hint_DPI_BLOCK: The server port answers, but even a plain TLS handshake with its SNI fails — a live REALITY server replies to that with its masking site. So the connection is throttled on the way and the key parameters are not at fault. Try the same key from a node in another country: if it works there, the block is on your segment.
xray_test.hint_KEY_PARAMS: The server is alive: it answers a plain TLS handshake with its masking site. So there is no block — the key parameters do not match: public key, short id, SNI or flow.

anti_ddos.title: Anti-DDoS
anti_ddos.subtitle: Emergency mode, attack auto-detection and whitelist across nodes
anti_ddos.autodetect_hint: Nodes enable protection themselves under attack; the panel maintains the whitelist and watchdog. Turning this off disables auto-detection on all nodes. It does NOT control emergency mode — that's separate, below.
anti_ddos.nodes_under_attack: Under attack: {{count}} of {{total}} nodes in emergency mode
anti_ddos.wl_auto_desc: All your server IPs and the panel IP are whitelisted automatically and pushed to nodes every hour. They always bypass the limits in emergency mode.
anti_ddos.wl_manual_desc: Add CDN subnets (e.g. Cloudflare) and other trusted IP/CIDR here, one per line. They are merged with the automatic part and pushed to nodes.
anti_ddos.src_desc: The panel periodically fetches these URLs and extracts IP/CIDR (JSON or plain text — e.g. tech.cdn.yandex.net/prefixes/yc.json or cloudflare.com/ips-v4). They feed the anti-DDoS whitelist and apply on a node only while emergency mode is on.

info_sections.title: Standby mode (default)
info_sections.body: In peacetime there are no per-IP limits — nodes run at full speed with no overhead and no risk of hurting legitimate clients.

info_sections.title: Emergency mode
info_sections.body: Turns on a firewall ruleset: SYNPROXY (validates the TCP handshake before a connection reaches the server — kills SYN floods from spoofed addresses), a per-IP new-connections-per-second limit and dropping of junk packets (the concurrent-connection cap was removed: it walked the conntrack table on every new packet, so it got expensive exactly during an attack, and it punished subscribers sharing a carrier NAT). Applied only to client ports (auto-detected); SSH and the panel port are never touched.

info_sections.title: Auto-detect (watchdog)
info_sections.body: Each node runs an independent watchdog that watches for attack signatures: conntrack table filling up, a spike in SYN-cookies, a flood of tiny packets, softirq load. On clear signs it enables emergency mode itself within seconds — without waiting for an admin — and clears it after 15 minutes of quiet. Thresholds are conservative, so an evening client peak won't trigger it. The panel installs and updates the watchdog on nodes automatically — as soon as a node is on the new image, protection appears by itself, no manual rollout needed. You can disable auto-detection any time: the master switch at the top does it across all nodes, the per-node "Auto-detect" toggle does one node; disabling lifts any active auto-protection and returns the node to normal.

info_sections.title: Manual pin
info_sections.body: The "I'm under attack" button turns on emergency mode manually. Auto-detect won't clear such a mode by itself — only an admin will. Handy when you learn about an attack before the watchdog does.

info_sections.title: Whitelist
info_sections.body: Your relays, the panel and CDN subnets always bypass every limit — otherwise the strict rules would hit your own infrastructure (a relay and a CDN arrive from the same IPs carrying thousands of clients). The list lives on the node's disk and survives reboots and panel downtime.

dnat_profiles.title: DNAT routing
dnat_profiles.subtitle: Kernel-level port forwarding on nodes (iptables nat) — no userspace proxy
dnat_profiles.name: Name
dnat_profiles.create_hint: A profile defines the complete forwarding rule set of a node: anything not in the profile is removed on sync.
dnat_profiles.no_profiles_hint: Create the first one with the “Create profile” button.
dnat_profiles.select_profile: Select a profile on the left

dnat_profiles.sync_all_tooltip: Push the profile to all linked servers
dnat_profiles.unlink_confirm: Unlink {{name}}? All DNAT rules will be removed from the node (an offline node gets this once it is back online).
dnat_profiles.disable_rule: Disable rule (kept in the profile, removed from the node)
dnat_profiles.target_ip_hint: Several comma-separated addresses — balancing across servers: the first linked server gets the first IP, the second — the second, then round-robin
dnat_profiles.mask_ttl_hint: The node rewrites the TTL of forwarded packets to 64 in both directions and clamps MSS to the MTU. Otherwise the node IP emits a mix of client-OS TTLs (50s from mobiles, 110s from Windows) — a recognisable NAT-relay tell for DPI. Client TCP fingerprints are not hidden — that needs a terminating proxy (HAProxy).
dnat_profiles.enabled_hint: Untick to pause the rule: it stays in the profile but is removed from the nodes and traffic is no longer forwarded. Tick again to re-apply it.
dnat_profiles.target_port_hint: 0 — keep the port the client used (for a range each port maps to the same port); a number — collapse the whole input into that port
dnat_profiles.masquerade_hint: On (default): the target sees connections from the node address and replies to it — always works, but the real client IP does not reach the target. Off: the target sees the real client IP, but replies go straight to the client bypassing the node and the connection fails — works only if the target routes replies back through this node (e.g. the node is its gateway in a private network).
dnat_profiles.balancer_hint: The rule has several target IPs: profile servers get them in turn by link order (# on the Servers tab), round-robin. Each node still forwards to a single address.
dnat_profiles.distribution_per_server_hint: Each profile node gets one IP from the list by link order (# on the Servers tab), round-robin; a new server joins the end and the others keep their addresses.
dnat_profiles.distribution_random_hint: Each node gets the whole list and spreads new connections across IPs randomly and evenly; a connection stays on its IP until it closes. No health checks — a dead target keeps getting its share until removed from the list.
dnat_profiles.distribution_round_robin_hint: Each node gets the whole list and hands out new connections strictly in turn: 1st → first IP, 2nd → second, … No health checks.
dnat_profiles.distribution_client_hash_hint: Each node gets the whole list; the IP is picked by hashing the client address — one client always lands on the same target while the list is unchanged (for protocols with several connections per client). Requires the xt_HMARK kernel module. No health checks.
dnat_profiles.ssh_warning: A rule captures the SSH port ({{port}}/tcp) — after apply SSH goes to the target
dnat_profiles.ssh_warning_long: One of the rules captures the SSH port ({{port}}/tcp): after apply, SSH connections to the node go to the target server instead of the node itself. Ignore this if SSH listens on another port.
dnat_profiles.how_it_works: Rules are applied in the node kernel (iptables nat/PREROUTING + MASQUERADE + FORWARD). The node API port ({{port}}/tcp) cannot be forwarded. Port ranges are forwarded as a whole; with target port 0 the ports are preserved. Replies flow back through the node, so traffic is counted in both directions.

dnat_profiles.validation_port_range: Range end must be at least the listen port and at most 65535
dnat_profiles.validation_target: Target IP — one IPv4 address or several separated by commas
